reason: Publish #162, which lets the default branch seed the caches the TypeScript gate reads. #160 made the pnpm store cache read-only because an injected required workflow only ever fires on pull_request and a PR-ref cache is private to that PR, leaving the restore correct but permanently cold. #162 adds the missing writer: the gate also accepts workflow_call with a seed-caches input, so a repo's rendered standards.yml can call this same file on push-to-default, which is the one ref every PR in the repo may read from. Reusing the gate's own file rather than a separate seeder keeps the cache keys to a single definition. Also namespaces the concurrency group, because in a called workflow github.workflow resolves to the caller's name and the previous bare group would have deadlocked against standards.yml's identical group. Inert on PR runs until the standards companion lands: seed-caches defaults false and inputs is null on a pull_request trigger. The preceding range was validated by the 2026-07-28 manual Renovate wave: 26 typecheck gate runs, zero OOM kills, against 7 exit-137 kills on the prior wave.
